Following suit: your lowest card of the led suit.
Leading: the lowest card of the suit you hold most of.

In the opening trick: your lowest spade, otherwise your highest card.
No card of the led suit: your highest card.
All 52 cards are dealt. Whoever holds the Ace of Spades leads it to open.
Follow the led suit if you can. If you can't, any card you play is a thulla.
Get rid of all your cards to escape. The last player still holding cards loses the round.

With two players left, the first thulla ends the round: whoever picks up is the {0}.
Rounds play to the last card even when the loser is certain.
When the loser is certain, the round ends straight away.
Before the lead, anyone may ask for the hand of the next active player; the first accepted request wins. That player escapes.
From the second trick, the leader may take the whole hand of the next active player before leading by tapping Ask for hand. If they accept, they escape.
Taking another player's hand is off.
The last player holding cards is the {0}.
The opening trick is played in turn from the Ace of Spades.
Everyone answers the opening Ace of Spades at the same time, within 10 seconds.
The opening trick never causes a pick-up; its cards go to the discard.
Careful: a thulla counts in the opening trick, so someone can pick up the opening pile.
After a thulla, play carries on around the table; at the end the highest card of the led suit picks up everything.
A thulla stops the trick at once; whoever played the highest card of the led suit picks up the pile.
Run out of a suit early: once you can't follow, every card of that suit someone leads lets you give a thulla.
Watch what others pick up. A pile someone takes tells you which suits they now hold.
Leading your highest card can leave you with the hand and no cards; keep a low card for later.
The round opens with the Ace of Spades, and its holder has to lead it (R12).
You hold a card of the led suit, so you have to play one of them (R18). Only those cards are lit.

Bhabhi: brother's wife; the loser's title.
Yakka, badshah, begum, ghulam: ace, king, queen, jack.
Nikal gaya, bach gaya: got away, escaped.
Haath: hand; also the right to lead ("haath mera hai").
Haath lena: to take another player's hand.
Hukum, paan, eent, chidi: spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs.
Thulla: the off-suit card that stops a trick (literally slang for a police officer).
You're asking {0} to hand over their {1} cards. If they accept, the cards join your hand and {0} sits out safe for the rest of the round. They can refuse.
